questions.question: A parcel of mass 20 kg (particle P) rests on a rough horizontal floor with coefficient of friction 0.3. A force of 200 N acts at 15 degrees to the horizontal (up and to the left) and a force of T N acts at 25 degrees to the horizontal (up and to the right), both in the same vertical plane. Find the smallest value of T for which P remains in equilibrium.
steps: Weight = 20 x 9.8 = 196 N. Resolve vertically: R + 200 sin 15 + T sin 25 = 196.
Horizontally, the 200 N force pulls P to the left with 200 cos 15 = 193.2 N, so P tends to move left.
For the smallest T, friction acts to the right at its limit: F = 0.3R.
Horizontal: T cos 25 + 0.3R = 200 cos 15, with R = 196 - 200 sin 15 - T sin 25.

questions.question: A particle is acted on by force F of magnitude 8 N acting on a bearing of 240 degrees and force G of magnitude 10 N acting due South. Given R = F + G, find the magnitude of R.
steps: Bearing 240 degrees: F = 8(sin 240, cos 240) in (East, North) = (-6.93, -4) N.
Due South: G = (0, -10) N.

questions.question: A particle is acted on by force F (8 N, bearing 240 degrees) and force G (10 N, due South), with R = F + G. Give the direction of R as a bearing to the nearest degree.
steps: R = (-6.93, -14) N: components 6.93 N West and 14 N South.
The direction is in the South-West quadrant.
Angle measured from South towards West: arctan(6.93/14) = 26.3 degrees.
Bearing = 180 + 26.3 = 206.3, so 206 degrees (nearest degree).

questions.question: Agatha is at position vector (11i + 11j) m at t = 0 and skates with constant velocity (3i - j) m s^-1, relative to the door O. Find her position vector at time t seconds.
steps: Position = initial position + velocity x time.

questions.question: Brionie is at (7i + 16j) m at t = 0 and skates with constant velocity (4i - 2j) m s^-1. Agatha passes through point P at t = 6 s, where her position is 29i + 5j m. Show that Brionie also passes through P and find the time when this occurs.
questions.answer: Brionie passes P (29i + 5j) at t = 5.5 s
steps: Brionie: r_B = (7 + 4t)i + (16 - 2t)j.
Solve 7 + 4t = 29 gives t = 5.5; and 16 - 2t = 5 also gives t = 5.5.
Both components agree at t = 5.5 s, so Brionie passes through P at t = 5.5 s (shown).

questions.question: At time t seconds Agatha is at A and Brionie is at B. Show that the vector AB = [(t - 4)i + (5 - t)j] m.
steps: AB = position of B - position of A = r_B - r_A.
AB = (t - 4)i + (5 - t)j m (shown).

questions.question: Using AB = [(t - 4)i + (5 - t)j] m for the two girls, find the distance between Agatha and Brionie when they are closest together.
steps: Minimum when d/dt = 4t - 18 = 0, so t = 4.5 s.
Minimum distance = sqrt(0.5) = 0.707 m (3 s.f.).

questions.question: A particle P of weight 5 N hangs on a light inextensible string OP, with O fixed. P is held in equilibrium by a force of magnitude F N perpendicular to the string, with OP at 60 degrees to the vertical. Find the value of F.
steps: Forces on P: weight 5 N down, tension T along the string towards O, and F perpendicular to the string.
Resolve perpendicular to the string: F = 5 sin 60 (the weight component perpendicular to the string).

questions.question: The particle P (weight 5 N) is held in equilibrium with OP at 60 degrees to the vertical by a force F perpendicular to the string. Find the tension in the string.
steps: Resolve along the string: T = 5 cos 60 (the component of the weight along the string).
Check: perpendicular component of weight balances F = 5 sin 60 from part (a).

questions.question: Particle P (mass 4 kg) on a rough plane inclined at alpha (tan alpha = 3/4) is joined by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley to particle Q (mass m kg) on a smooth plane inclined at beta (tan beta = 4/3). The coefficient of friction between P and its plane is 1/4 and the system is in limiting equilibrium with P on the point of slipping down the first plane. Find m.
steps: sin alpha = 3/5, cos alpha = 4/5; sin beta = 4/5, cos beta = 3/5.
Normal reaction on P: R = 4 x 9.8 x 4/5 = 31.36 N, so limiting friction F = (1/4)(31.36) = 7.84 N acts up the plane.
For P (slipping down): T + 7.84 = 4 x 9.8 x 3/5 = 23.52, so T = 15.68 N.
For Q (smooth plane, pulled up the plane): T = m x 9.8 x sin beta = m x 7.84.

questions.question: Using the system in part (a) (P on the first plane, Q on the second plane, string over the pulley at the intersection of the planes), find the magnitude of the force exerted on the pulley by the string.
steps: Tension in the string is T = 15.68 N (from part (a)).
Since alpha + beta = 90 degrees (tan alpha = 3/4, tan beta = 4/3), the two string segments are perpendicular.
The force on the pulley is the vector sum of two equal tensions at 90 degrees.
Magnitude = T sqrt(2) = 15.68 x 1.414 = 22.2 N (3 s.f.).

questions.question: Find the direction of the force exerted on the pulley by the string in the system of part (b).
questions.answer: Vertically downwards, tilted about 8.1 degrees towards P (to the left), i.e. 81.9 degrees below the horizontal.
steps: Take the segments from the pulley: towards P (-cos alpha, -sin alpha) = (-0.8, -0.6) and towards Q (cos beta, -sin beta) = (0.6, -0.8).
Sum with equal tensions 15.68 N: 15.68(-0.2, -1.4).
Direction is downwards and to the left (towards P): angle from the vertical = arctan(0.2/1.4) = 8.1 degrees.
